source: R 4.4.0 metafor::rma(test = "knha") Monte Carlo, evaluated independently of SciPy and of the PowerBench simulator
purpose: Adjudicates the Hartung-Knapp random-effects reference. Guards against regression to the pre-2026-08-03 implementation, which combined three defects that partially offset: df = k - 2 instead of k - 1, no Hartung-Knapp variance rescaling, and a t critical value evaluated against a normal rejection probability.

design.tau_squared: fixed at the known value, matching the PowerBench planning contract
design.test: Hartung-Knapp adjusted random-effects summary, t reference with k - 1 df

cases.label: Hartung-Knapp adjusted test, the method PowerBench claims to implement
cases.note: PowerBench reference gives 0.8000 and its simulator gives 0.7990 at this N. All three agree within Monte Carlo error (400 replications give an MC SE of about 0.02).

cases.label: unadjusted inverse-variance test, recorded to show what the HK adjustment costs
cases.note: Not the method PowerBench implements. Recorded because the difference (0.92 vs 0.79) is exactly the magnitude of the error the pre-fix hybrid produced, so a future regression toward the unadjusted test is easy to recognise.

q_statistic_check.note: The Hartung-Knapp rescaling factor q = sum_i w_i (y_i - mu)^2 / (k - 1) must have E[q] = 1 and follow chi-square_{k-1}/(k-1); this is what makes the summary statistic non-central t and licenses the closed-form power expression.
